lines.say: Why does soreness hit two days later, not right after?
Why does this happen, number thirteen.
It's called D O M S. Delayed onset muscle soreness.
Hard or new training causes tiny damage in your muscle.
Then your body starts repairing. Swelling and chemicals from that repair make your nerves extra sensitive.
That process builds up slowly, so soreness peaks one to three days later.
The lowering part of a rep causes the most. That's why going down stairs after leg day hurts.
Do the same workout again, and you get much less sore. Your muscle adapts fast.
